ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02710 is refunded in full to the rider. The driver is paid nothing, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Why. The pickup was the Bedok Interchange PHV bay, a TRANSPORT_HUB, so the arrival radius is 150 m (POL-NS-02, read off EV-TRIP-02710). The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02710, weight 1.0, 100% coverage and no gaps) contains 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes across the whole trip and his closest approach to the pin is 517.4 m. The 'arrived' marker he set at 22:48:55 therefore places him more than 300 m from the pin and, with speeds of 28.8–63.0 km/h in the same trace, still in motion: under POL-NS-05 the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputing from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, there is none anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) applies — full refund of the SGD 4.50, no compensation, and the false-arrival referral above. POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the same evidence (the driver was never inside the 150 m geofence), and independently POL-NS-06 gives the same full refund because the in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (EV-TRIP-02710.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) — a 180-second shortfall.

Driver's advocate's claims. The wrong-entrance argument under POL-NS-03 is rejected: that clause requires the driver to be stationary within 400 m of the pin, and his minimum distance is 517.4 m, so the ceiling is not met and no goodwill payment arises. The driver's statement 'I arrived and waited, the rider did not come' is contradicted by his own telemetry (517 m to 5.2 km from the pin across the window) and is outweighed by it. The rider's presence on her own track (54 of 54 fixes qualifying inside the 200 m hub radius, mean 5.4 m) is accepted as a fact, but it does not by itself decide anything.

Rider's advocate's POL-NS-04 claims are rejected on their merits. Limbs (a) and (c) are met (locating message at 22:49:35; rider within 200 m throughout), but limb (b) fails: the driver DID reply in the chat at 22:50:05, 30 seconds after her message, and POL-NS-04 does not apply where the driver replied within 120 seconds, whatever the reply says. That clause therefore adds nothing here — the refund comes from POL-NS-05(ii), POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 instead — and its failure changes no amount.

On compensation: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 93 completed trips, a rate of 0.0215, both below the clause's thresholds), but the driver receives nothing because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 leaves the fee standing.

No escalation arises. The trace is complete, the chat log and fare ledger reconcile to the SGD 4.50 net fee, there is no clock skew, the arrival-marker conflict between the trip record and the trace is resolved by POL-NS-05, the counterparty-dispute counters are 0 and no profile trigger fires. Confidence is capped at 1.0 by the artifacts carrying the deciding facts (all at weight 1.0) and is set at 0.93. Nothing rests on the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02710-01, weight 0.0); the two claims that cited it without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT code were discarded by the referee.

The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05) and so executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record: record trip TRP-02710 against driver DRV-09710 as a false-arrival event — the 22:48:55 'arrived' marker is false (the trace places the driver at least 517.4 m from the pickup pin and shows him moving at 28.8–63.0 km/h) and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.
